problem: Prior ObjectNav methods learn an association (e.g. relation graph) between visual input and goal from training environments. This experience helps when test layouts resemble training but hurts when the layout gap is large.
motivation: Agents deployed in unseen environments need to keep useful prior knowledge while suppressing it when the test layout differs from training. The paper measures how far the test layout is from the learned prior and uses that gap to control the experience's effect on the policy.
key_idea: Compute a layout gap as the KL divergence between posterior and prior object-layout distributions, and use it in a soft Total Direct Effect (L-sTDE) causal-inference step to adjust the navigation policy's prediction.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract's claim is that the experience's effect on the policy should be weighted by how far the current layout is from training. This is done softly rather than by removing the experience outright.
method: Layout gap: KL divergence between the posterior and prior distributions of object layout, used to measure the mismatch between the test environment and training experience.
L-sTDE: a layout-based soft Total Direct Effect framework from causal inference that adjusts the navigation policy's prediction.
Soft TDE (sTDE): scales how much of the experience effect is removed according to the layout gap, keeping the positive effect and removing the negative one.

setting.backbone: not specified in the abstract (applied on top of existing learned ObjectNav policies)

results: The abstract reports only that experiments on AI2THOR, RoboTHOR and Habitat demonstrate effectiveness. It gives no numbers or named baselines.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details of the setting and results are unknown.
